data.long_meaning: Owais is a name that symbolizes strength, courage, and loyalty. It is also associated with Owais al-Qarni, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). The name Owais carries the meaning “Little Wolf” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Owais usually hope their child will grow to embody little wolf and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Owais belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Little Wolf.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Owais total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_english.name: Owais
in_english.long_meaning: Owais is derived from the Arabic root 'A-w-s', meaning 'sign' or 'mark'. In Islamic tradition, Owais al-Qarani was a notable companion of Prophet Muhammad who embraced Islam before the Prophet's passing. The name symbolizes spiritual significance, good character, and devotion. It is popular across various Muslim cultures for its historical and religious connotations.

It is derived from the name 'Uways ibn 'Amir, a notable figure in the Early Muslim History, considered the first freed slave Sahabi (Companion of the Prophet Muhammad PBUH). His embrace of Islam and his exceptional courage and loyalty to the Muslim cause remain an inspirational account in Islamic history. The name Owais is often given to children as a reminder of these values.
